sections.heading: Broken down, flat, or damaged.
sections.body: Our 24 hour tow service can get you out of a jam when you need it. If your vehicle breaks down or becomes disabled in an accident, call the 24 hour number and a licensed tow truck driver is sent to your location.

sections.heading: Wreckers and emergency towing.
sections.body: Tow trucks, wreckers and emergency towing across Dallas. Emergency work is the bulk of what we do, which is why the line is answered around the clock rather than during office hours.

sections.heading: The location matters as much as the vehicle.
sections.body: A car on a driveway and the same car on the shoulder of a highway are different jobs. Traffic, barriers, soft ground and low clearance all change which truck can actually reach it and how long the recovery takes. Saying where you are precisely — the road, the direction of travel, the nearest exit — gets the right truck moving sooner than a postcode does.

sections.heading: Location is the part people get wrong.
sections.body: A street name is enough in a neighbourhood and close to useless on a highway, where the same road runs for miles in both directions. Exit numbers, mile markers, the last sign you passed and which direction you were travelling all narrow it down far faster. If your phone can share a pin, that settles it outright. The second thing worth having ready is where the vehicle is going, because a tow to a shop across town and a tow to your driveway are different jobs to quote and to plan. And if the car will not shift out of park, the keys are missing, or it is boxed in, say so on the call rather than when the driver is standing next to it.

faqs.q: Flatbed or a regular tow truck?
faqs.a: A flatbed carries the vehicle with all four wheels off the road, which is what you want for all-wheel drive, low ground clearance, a car with damaged wheels, or anything you would rather not have rolling behind a truck. A conventional tow truck lifts one end and is quicker to hook up. Say what you are driving and dispatch can pick.

faqs.q: Can you get to a vehicle in a parking garage?
faqs.a: Low clearance is the deciding factor and it is worth mentioning on the call, because a flatbed that cannot get under the entrance is a wasted trip for both of us. If you know the height limit posted at the entrance, that single number answers most of the question.

pages.heading: Roadside assistance across Dallas.
pages.intro: Not every problem needs a tow. Often the quicker answer is getting the vehicle running again where it sits.
pages.seoTitle: Roadside Assistance Dallas TX | 24 Hour Towing Dallas
pages.seoDescription: Roadside assistance in Dallas, Texas — tire changes, jumpstarts and help getting a disabled vehicle back on the road, 24 hours a day.

sections.heading: Back on the road, not on a truck.
sections.body: From having a tire changed to jumpstarting your car, roadside assistance is about getting the vehicle moving again rather than hauling it somewhere. When that is the faster fix, it is the cheaper one too.

sections.heading: Dispatched from the same 24 hour line.
sections.body: Roadside calls run through the same dispatch as the tow trucks, so there is one number to remember whichever of the two you turn out to need.

sections.heading: Get clear of the traffic side.
sections.body: If you are on a live carriageway, the safest place is usually out of the vehicle and behind a barrier, not sitting in the driver's seat. If the car is somewhere you cannot safely leave it, say so when you call — it changes how urgently the job is treated.

sections.heading: Some problems move with the vehicle.
sections.body: Roadside work is for things that can be put right where the car sits: a flat with a usable spare, a dead battery, an empty tank, keys locked inside. Those are quick and nothing has to be transported. Other problems only look like roadside jobs. A flat with no spare, a shredded sidewall, a car that starts and immediately dies again, or anything involving the transmission means the vehicle has to move regardless. Knowing which one you have before a truck is dispatched saves a trip that cannot fix anything. If you are not sure, describe the symptoms on the call — what happened, what it sounded like, whether anything still works — and dispatch can usually tell which way it will go.

faqs.q: Is roadside help cheaper than a tow?
faqs.a: Usually, because nothing is being transported — but only when the problem is actually fixable at the roadside. A flat tire with a usable spare, a dead battery, or an empty tank are roadside jobs. A failed transmission is not. If it turns out the vehicle has to move, it is better to know that before a truck is dispatched.

faqs.q: What if I have no spare tire?
faqs.a: Then the vehicle needs to move rather than be fixed where it sits, because there is nothing to fit. Plenty of newer cars ship with a sealant kit instead of a spare, which handles a puncture but not a sidewall tear or a blowout. Check before you call — it changes which truck comes out.

pages.heading: Battery jumpstarts and replacement.
pages.intro: A dead battery does not have to end the day. We can jump it where it sits, or replace it and have you moving again.
pages.seoTitle: Car Battery Jumpstart & Replacement Dallas TX | 24 Hour Towing Dallas
pages.seoDescription: Car battery jumpstarts and replacement in Dallas, Texas. Jumper boxes mean a dead battery can be started wherever the car is parked.

sections.heading: Two ways out of a dead battery.
sections.body: As one of our roadside assistance services, we can replace or jumpstart your car's dead battery. A licensed driver is sent out and will either provide a jumpstart or fit a new battery, changing it out on the spot.

sections.kicker: Why it matters who does it
sections.heading: Jumping a car wrong can cost you an ECU.
sections.body: We are equipped with jumper boxes, so a dead battery can be started regardless of where the car is parked. It is worth saying that jumping a vehicle has to be done correctly — done incorrectly it can damage the car’s computer, which is a far more expensive problem than the battery was.

sections.kicker: When a jump will not hold
sections.heading: A battery that dies twice is not a flat battery.
sections.body: If a car starts on a jump and dies again shortly after, the battery is usually not the fault — it is more often the alternator failing to recharge it. Worth knowing before paying for a replacement battery that will be flat again by the end of the week.

sections.heading: What happens after the jump tells you.
sections.body: A jump start puts enough charge in to turn the engine over. What happens next is the diagnosis. If the car runs and keeps running, the battery was drained — lights left on, a door not shut, a short trip that never let it recover — and it will likely charge back up as you drive. If it starts and then dies again within minutes, the charging system is not doing its job, and a second jump buys the same few minutes as the first. Either way, get it somewhere it can be tested rather than relying on repeat jumps. A battery that has been run flat several times rarely comes back to full health even once the underlying fault is found.

faqs.q: Will a jump start fix it, or do I need a battery?
faqs.a: A jump gets the engine running. Whether it stays running is the real test: if the car starts and then dies again shortly after, the battery is not holding charge or the alternator is not charging it, and a second jump only buys the same few minutes. A jump that holds usually means the battery was drained rather than dead.

pages.heading: We buy junk cars.
pages.intro: If the vehicle is not worth recovering, we will take it off your hands rather than tow it somewhere you have to deal with it again.
pages.seoTitle: We Buy Junk Cars Dallas TX | 24 Hour Towing Dallas
pages.seoDescription: Junk car removal in Dallas, Texas. We buy junk cars and haul them away, so a vehicle that is not worth repairing stops being your problem.

sections.kicker: When it is the right call
sections.heading: Some vehicles are not worth the tow.
sections.body: A car that will cost more to repair than it is worth does not need recovering to a shop. Removing it is usually the cheaper end to the story, and it clears the driveway or the yard at the same time.

sections.heading: Title and location.
sections.body: The two things that decide whether a junk car can be collected are whether you hold the title and whether the vehicle can be reached by a truck. A car with no title, or one boxed in behind two others in a garage, is a different job — not impossible, just worth mentioning on the phone rather than on the day.

sections.heading: Whether it rolls matters more than whether it runs.
sections.body: Non-running is normal — that is most of what gets collected. The questions that actually change the equipment are different ones. Does it still roll, or are the wheels gone or seized? Is it reachable, or is it behind a gate, up against a fence, or boxed in by other vehicles? Has it sunk into soft ground after sitting through a few seasons? A car that can be winched straight onto a bed is a simple job; one that has to be dragged out of a back yard past two other vehicles is not, and finding that out on arrival helps nobody. Mention ownership paperwork on the call too, since that usually needs to be sorted before anything moves.

pages.ctaHeadline: Got a car to get rid of?

faqs.q: Does the car need to run?
faqs.a: No. Non-running, wrecked, flood-damaged and long-dead vehicles are all removable. What matters more than whether it starts is whether it can be reached and whether it rolls — a car with no wheels, or one boxed in behind other vehicles, needs different equipment. Mention that when you call.

Where the truck starts from matters for how long it takes, so ask on the call if timing is the deciding factor.

sections.heading: Weight is what decides it.
sections.body: A standard tow truck is built for cars and light pickups. Once the vehicle is a box truck, a bus, a motorhome or a tractor unit, the job needs a wrecker: heavier boom, heavier winch, and a chassis rated to lift it without being dragged around by it. Putting the wrong truck on a heavy recovery is how both vehicles end up damaged.

sections.heading: Three things decide which truck we send.
sections.body: What the vehicle is, roughly what it weighs, and what the access is like. A tractor unit on a hard shoulder and the same unit in a soft yard are different jobs needing different equipment. Getting that right on the phone is the difference between one truck arriving and two.

sections.heading: Heavy breakdowns do not keep hours.
sections.body: Commercial vehicles break down on schedules, which means at night and at weekends as often as not. Wrecker work runs through the same 24-hour dispatch as everything else, so there is one number whichever kind of truck you turn out to need.

sections.heading: Where the vehicle sits changes the job.
sections.body: Weight decides which truck, but access decides how the recovery is done. The same tractor unit on a hard shoulder and in a soft yard are two different jobs: one is a straightforward hookup, the other may need winching before anything can be lifted, and possibly room to work that is not there. Overhead clearance, the surface underfoot, how much space there is to bring a truck alongside, and whether the vehicle can roll at all are all worth describing on the call. It is the difference between one truck arriving prepared and a second having to be sent. If you can send a photograph of the position, that answers more than a description usually can.

faqs.q: Is heavy hauling your main business?
faqs.a: No — most of the work is cars and light pickups, and that is what the fleet is built around. Heavy and wrecker work is genuinely offered rather than advertised for its own sake, which is worth saying plainly: if you are moving a tractor unit, describe the job properly on the call so dispatch can tell you straight away whether it is one we should take.

faqs.q: What should I have ready when I call about a heavy vehicle?
faqs.a: What the vehicle is, roughly what it weighs, whether it still rolls, and what the access is like — surface underfoot, overhead clearance, and how much room there is to bring a truck alongside. A photograph of how it is sitting answers more than a description usually can. Those details decide which truck comes out, and getting them right is the difference between one truck arriving prepared and a second having to follow.

faqHeading: What people ask before they call.

faqs.q: What decides the cost of a tow?
faqs.a: Mainly the distance, the type of vehicle, and how hard it is to reach. A car on a driveway and the same car nosed into a ditch are different jobs, because one is a hookup and the other is a recovery. Time of day can matter too. Ask for the figure when you call, with the vehicle and the location in front of you — that is when it can actually be answered.

Yes — drivers are licensed and the operation is insured. It is a fair thing to ask before handing over a vehicle, and worth asking of anyone you call, because a tow means someone else takes custody of something valuable of yours for the length of the journey.

Yes. Dispatch runs 24 hours a day, every day, which is the whole point of the number. Breakdowns and accidents do not keep business hours, and a towing company that only answers in the daytime is not much use at the moment you need one.

faqs.q: What should I tell dispatch when I call?
faqs.a: Four things get the right truck moving: where you are, what you are driving, what is wrong with it, and where you want it taken. Cross streets, a mile marker or an exit number beat a street name on a highway. If the car will not shift out of park, or the keys are gone, say so on the call rather than when the driver arrives.

faqs.q: Should I wait in the vehicle?
faqs.a: On a highway, no. If you can get out safely on the side away from traffic and wait behind a barrier, that is the safer place to be — a stopped vehicle on a shoulder is a target. Put the hazards on, and if you have cones or triangles, set them out behind. On a quiet residential street, staying in the car with the doors locked is usually fine.

faqs.q: Can you tow a car that will not start or has no keys?
faqs.a: Yes. Cars that will not start, will not shift, have a flat battery, or have seized brakes get moved regularly — that is most of the work. Tell dispatch on the call so the right equipment comes out the first time. A car that cannot roll needs a different approach from one that can.

faqs.q: Can you take it to my own mechanic?
faqs.a: Yes. It is your vehicle and your choice of destination — a shop, a dealership, your home, or a body shop after an accident. Have the address ready when you call. If you are not sure where you want it yet, say so, because that changes what the driver needs to know.

faqs.q: Do I need the title to have a junk car removed?
faqs.a: In most cases you need to show you own the vehicle before it can be taken away, and the title is the usual way to do that. Rules vary by situation, so it is worth raising on the call rather than at the kerb. Also mention if the car is behind a gate, blocked in, or has no wheels, because that changes the equipment.
